title.zh: 卷一百二十四 列傳第十二 擴廓帖木兒 陳友定 把匝剌瓦爾密
title.en: Volume 124 Biographies 12: Kuokuotiemuer, Chen Youding, Bazalawaermi
title.raw: 卷一百二十四 列傳第十二 擴廓帖木兒 陳友定 把匝剌瓦爾密 Volume 124 Biographies 12: Kuokuotiemuer, Chen Youding, Bazalawaermi

sentences.zh: 擴廓帖木兒附:蔡子英 陳友定附:伯顏子中 等 把匝剌瓦爾密

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemuer, with appended biography: Cai Ziying; Chen Youding, with appended biography: Bayan Zizhong, et al.; Bazalawaermi.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemuer (with appended biography of Cai Ziying); Chen Youding (with appended biography of Bayan Zizhong and others); Bazalawaermi.

sentences.zh: 擴廓帖木兒

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemuer.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemuer

sentences.zh: 擴廓帖木兒，沈丘人。

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemuer was a man of Shenqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemuer was a native of Shenqiu.

sentences.zh: 本王姓，小字保保，元平章察罕帖木兒甥也。

translations.literal: His original surname was Wang; his childhood name was Baobao; he was the nephew of the Yuan Grand Councillor Chaghan Temur.
translations.idiomatic: He was born into the Wang clan and was known in youth as Baobao; he was the nephew of Chaghan Temur, a Yuan grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 察罕養為子，順帝賜名擴廓帖木兒。

translations.literal: Chaghan adopted him as a son, and Emperor Shundi bestowed upon him the name Kuokuotiemuer.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temur raised him as his own son, and Emperor Shundi gave him the name Kuokuotiemuer.

sentences.zh: 汝、潁盜起，中原大亂，元師久無功。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Ru and Ying; the Central Plains fell into great disorder; Yuan troops for a long time achieved no success.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels broke out in the Ru and Ying region, the Central Plains plunged into chaos, and Yuan armies went for years without a decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年，察罕起義兵，戰河南、北，擊賊關中、河東，復汴梁，走劉福通，平山東，降田豐，滅賊幾盡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng, Chaghan raised righteous troops, fought in Henan and the north, struck bandits in Guanzhong and Hedong, recovered Bianliang, drove off Liu Futong, pacified Shandong, induced Tian Feng to surrender, and nearly exterminated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng year 12 (1352), Chaghan Temur raised a loyalist army, campaigned across Henan and the north, crushed rebels in Guanzhong and Hedong, retook Bianliang (Kaifeng), routed Liu Futong, pacified Shandong, won Tian Feng's submission, and all but wiped out the rebel forces.

sentences.zh: 既而總大軍圍益都，田豐叛，察罕為王士誠所刺，事具《元史》。

translations.literal: Thereafter he led a great army to besiege Yidu; Tian Feng rebelled; Chaghan was assassinated by Zhang Shicheng—the full account is in the History of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then massed his forces to besiege Yidu, but Tian Feng turned traitor, and Chaghan Temur was assassinated by agents of Zhang Shicheng; the details are recorded in the History of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 察罕既死，順帝即軍中拜擴廓太尉、中書平章政事、知樞密院事，如察罕官。

translations.literal: After Chaghan died, Emperor Shundi immediately in the army appointed Kuokuotiemuer Grand Guardian, Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat, and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs—the same offices Chaghan had held.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Chaghan Temur died, Emperor Shundi promoted Kuokuotiemuer in camp to grand guardian, grand councillor of the Central Secretariat, and commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs—the same posts his adoptive father had held.

sentences.zh: 帥兵圍益都，穴地而入，克之。

translations.literal: He led troops to besiege Yidu, tunneled into the city, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He led his army to besiege Yidu, broke in through underground tunnels, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 執豐、士誠，剖其心以祭察罕，縛陳猱頭等二十余人獻闕下。

translations.literal: He seized Feng and Shicheng, cut out their hearts to sacrifice to Chaghan, and bound Chen Maotou and more than twenty others to present at the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Tian Feng and Zhang Shicheng, cut out their hearts as offerings to Chaghan Temur's spirit, and sent more than twenty captives—including Chen Maotou—in bonds to the capital.

sentences.zh: 東取莒州，山東地悉定。

translations.literal: He took Juzhou to the east, and all Shandong was settled.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed east to take Juzhou, bringing all of Shandong under control.

sentences.zh: 至正二十二年也。

translations.literal: This was in the twenty-second year of Zhizheng.
translations.idiomatic: This took place in Zhizheng year 22 (1362).

sentences.zh: 初，察罕定晉、冀，孛羅帖木兒在大同，以兵爭其地，數相攻，朝廷下詔和解，終不聽。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chaghan had secured Jin and Ji, Boluo Temur was at Datong and fought with troops over that territory; they attacked each other repeatedly; the court issued edicts to reconcile them, but in the end they would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Chaghan Temur had secured Shanxi and Hebei, Boluo Temur held Datong and repeatedly clashed with him over those lands; though the court ordered them to make peace, neither side would comply.

sentences.zh: 擴廓既平齊地，引軍還，駐太原，與孛羅構難如故。

translations.literal: After Kuokuotiemuer had pacified Qi territory, he led the army back and encamped at Taiyuan; his feud with Boluo was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Once Kuokuotiemuer had pacified Shandong, he withdrew his army and encamped at Taiyuan, where his feud with Boluo Temur resumed unchanged.

sentences.zh: 會朝臣老的沙、禿堅獲罪于太子，出奔孛羅，孛羅匿之。

translations.literal: It happened that court ministers Laodisha and Tujian had offended the crown prince and fled to Boluo; Boluo concealed them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the courtiers Laodisha and Tujian had fallen afoul of the crown prince and fled to Boluo Temur, who sheltered them in secret.

sentences.zh: 詔削孛羅官，解其兵柄。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Boluo of his offices and relieved him of military command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict stripping Boluo Temur of his rank and relieving him of command over his troops.

sentences.zh: 孛羅遂舉兵反，犯京師，殺丞相搠思監，自為左丞相，老的沙為平章，禿堅知樞密院。

translations.literal: Boluo then raised troops in rebellion, invaded the capital, killed the chief councillor Tosi Temur, made himself left chief councillor, appointed Laodisha grand councillor, and Tujian commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Boluo Temur then rebelled, marched on the capital, killed Chief Councillor Tosi Temur, installed himself as left chief councillor, made Laodisha a grand councillor, and put Tujian in charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 太子求援于擴廓，擴廓遣其將白鎖住以萬騎入衛，戰不利，奉太子奔太原。

translations.literal: The crown prince sought aid from Kuokuotiemuer; Kuokuotiemuer sent his general Bai Suozhu with ten thousand horsemen to guard the capital; the battle went badly, and he escorted the crown prince in flight to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince appealed to Kuokuotiemuer for help; he sent his general Bai Suozhu with ten thousand cavalry to defend the capital, but after a defeat escorted the prince in flight to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 逾年，擴廓以太子令舉兵討孛羅，入大同，進薄大都。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Kuokuotiemuer, by the crown prince's order, raised troops to attack Boluo, entered Datong, and advanced to press upon Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, acting on the crown prince's orders, Kuokuotiemuer marched against Boluo Temur, entered Datong, and pressed toward Dadu.

sentences.zh: 順帝乃襲殺孛羅於朝。

translations.literal: Emperor Shundi then had Boluo assassinated at court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shundi then had Boluo Temur killed by surprise at court.

sentences.zh: 擴廓從太子入覲，以為太傅、左丞相。

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemuer followed the crown prince to audience and was made Grand Tutor and left chief councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemuer accompanied the crown prince to an audience with the emperor and was appointed grand tutor and left chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 當是時，微擴廓，太子幾殆。

translations.literal: At that time, but for Kuokuotiemuer, the crown prince would nearly have perished.
translations.idiomatic: At that juncture, had it not been for Kuokuotiemuer, the crown prince would almost certainly have been lost.

sentences.zh: 擴廓功雖高，起行間，驟至相位，中朝舊臣多忌之者。

translations.literal: Though Kuokuotiemuer's merit was great, he had risen from the ranks and suddenly reached the highest office; many old ministers at court envied him.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were great, but he had risen from the army to the highest office overnight, and many long-serving courtiers resented him.

sentences.zh: 而擴廓久典軍，亦不樂在內，居兩月，即請出治兵，南平江、淮。

translations.literal: Moreover, Kuokuotiemuer had long commanded armies and was not happy within; after two months he at once requested to go out and manage troops, to pacify the south along the Yangzi and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemuer, who had spent his career in the field, was ill at ease at court; after only two months he asked leave to take command again and pacify the Yangzi and Huai regions in the south.

sentences.zh: 詔許之，封河南王，俾總天下兵，代皇太子出征，分省中官屬之半以自隨。

translations.literal: An edict approved this; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Henan, made to command all troops under heaven, to campaign in place of the crown prince, and given half the officials of the Secretariat to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, enfeoffed him as Prince of Henan, put all armies under his command, and sent him to campaign in the crown prince's stead, with half the Secretariat's staff assigned to his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 鹵簿甲仗互數十里，軍容甚盛。

translations.literal: Imperial guards and armor stretched for several tens of li; the military display was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: His imperial escort and armaments stretched for miles, and the spectacle of his army was magnificent.

sentences.zh: 時太祖已滅陳友諒，盡有江、楚地，張士誠據淮東、浙西。

translations.literal: At that time the founding emperor had already destroyed Chen Youliang and held all Jiang and Chu territory; Zhang Shicheng held Huaidong and western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Ming founder had destroyed Chen Youliang and held the Yangzi and Chu regions; Zhang Shicheng controlled the Huai east and western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 擴廓知南軍強，未可輕進，乃駐軍河南，檄關中四將軍會師大舉。

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemuer knew the southern armies were strong and could not be lightly advanced upon; he therefore encamped in Henan and issued summons to the four generals of Guanzhong to join forces for a great campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the southern forces were formidable, Kuokuotiemuer would not risk a hasty advance; he encamped in Henan and called on the four Guanzhong generals to muster for a major offensive.

sentences.zh: 四將軍者，李思齊、張思道、孔興、脫列伯也。

translations.literal: The four generals were Li Siqi, Zhang Sidao, Kong Xing, and Tuoliebo.
translations.idiomatic: These four generals were Li Siqi, Zhang Sidao, Kong Xing, and Tuoliebo.

sentences.zh: 思齊，羅山人，與察罕同起義兵，齒位略相埒。

translations.literal: Siqi was a man of Luoshan; he had raised righteous troops together with Chaghan, and their seniority and standing were roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siqi was from Luoshan; he had raised loyalist forces alongside Chaghan Temur, and the two men were peers in seniority and standing.

sentences.zh: 得檄大怒曰：「吾與若父交，若發未燥，敢檄我耶！

translations.literal: Receiving the summons, he flew into a rage and said: I was friends with your father; your hair is not yet dry—how dare you summon me!
translations.idiomatic: When the summons arrived, he flew into a rage: "I was friends with your father! Your hair is scarcely dry—how dare you order me about!"

sentences.zh: 」令其下一甲不得出武關。

translations.literal: He ordered that not a single soldier under him might pass out of Wuguan.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that not one of his companies was to march through Wuguan Pass.

sentences.zh: 思道等亦皆不聽調。

translations.literal: Sidao and the others likewise all refused to obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sidao and the others likewise refused to answer his call.

sentences.zh: 擴廓歎曰：「吾奉詔總天下兵，而鎮將不受節制，何討賊為！

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemuer sighed and said: I have received the edict to command all troops under heaven, yet frontier generals will not accept my control—how can I campaign against bandits!
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemuer sighed: "I have been ordered to command all armies under heaven, yet the regional commanders will not obey me—how am I to fight the rebels?"

sentences.zh: 」乃遣其弟脫因帖木兒以一軍屯濟南，防遏南軍，而自引兵西入關，攻思齊等。

translations.literal: He then sent his younger brother Tuoyintiemuer with one army to encamp at Jinan to block the southern forces, while he himself led troops west into the passes to attack Siqi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his younger brother Tuoyintiemuer with one corps to hold Jinan against the southern armies, while he himself marched west through the passes to attack Li Siqi and his allies.

sentences.zh: 思齊等會兵長安，盟於含元殿舊基，並力拒擴廓。

translations.literal: Siqi and the others gathered troops at Chang'an, allied at the old site of the Hanyuan Hall, and joined forces to resist Kuokuotiemuer.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siqi and his allies massed at Chang'an, swore their pact on the ruins of the Hanyuan Hall, and united to resist Kuokuotiemuer.

sentences.zh: 相持經年，數百戰未能決。

translations.literal: They faced each other for more than a year; hundreds of battles could not decide the outcome.
translations.idiomatic: The stalemate lasted more than a year, with hundreds of engagements yet no decisive outcome.

sentences.zh: 順帝使使諭令罷兵，專事江、淮。

translations.literal: Emperor Shundi sent envoys instructing them to cease fighting and devote themselves solely to the Yangzi and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shundi sent envoys ordering them to halt the internecine war and focus on the Yangzi and Huai fronts.

sentences.zh: 擴廓欲遂定思齊等，然後引軍東。

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemuer wished first to settle Siqi and the others, then lead the army east.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemuer wanted to finish off Li Siqi and his allies first, then turn his army eastward.

sentences.zh: 乃遣其驍將貊高趨河中，欲出不意搗鳳翔，覆思齊巢穴。

translations.literal: He then sent his fierce general Mo Gao to hurry toward Hezhong, intending by surprise to strike Fengxiang and overturn Siqi's nest.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched his fierce general Mo Gao toward Hezhong, planning a surprise thrust against Fengxiang to destroy Li Siqi's base.

sentences.zh: 貊高所將多孛羅部曲，行至衛輝，軍變，脅貊高叛擴廓，襲衛輝、彰德據之，罪狀擴廓於朝。

translations.literal: Most of those Mo Gao led were Boluo's former troops; when they reached Weihui the army mutinied, coerced Mo Gao to rebel against Kuokuotiemuer, seized Weihui and Zhangde, and denounced Kuokuotiemuer at court.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Mo Gao's troops were veterans of Boluo Temur's command; at Weihui they mutinied, forced Mo Gao to turn against Kuokuotiemuer, seized Weihui and Zhangde, and laid charges against him at court.

sentences.zh: 初，太子之奔太原也，欲用唐肅宗靈武故事自立。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the crown prince fled to Taiyuan, he wished to follow the Tang precedent of Emperor Suzong at Lingwu and establish himself independently.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince had fled to Taiyuan, he had wanted to follow the Tang precedent of Emperor Suzong proclaiming himself at Lingwu and set up an independent regime.

sentences.zh: 擴廓不可。

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemuer would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemuer would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 及還京師，皇后諭指令以重兵擁太子入城，脅順帝禪位。

translations.literal: When they returned to the capital, the empress instructed him to bring the crown prince into the city with a heavy force and coerce Emperor Shundi to abdicate.
translations.idiomatic: On their return to the capital, the empress instructed him to march the crown prince into the city at the head of a large army and force Emperor Shundi to abdicate.

sentences.zh: 擴廓未至京三十里，留其軍，以數騎入朝。

translations.literal: When Kuokuotiemuer was still thirty li from the capital, he left his army and entered court with only a few horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li short of the capital, Kuokuotiemuer left his army behind and rode into court with only a small escort.

sentences.zh: 由是太子銜之，而順帝亦心忌擴廓。

translations.literal: Because of this the crown prince bore a grudge against him, and Emperor Shundi also harbored suspicion in his heart toward Kuokuotiemuer.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince never forgave him for this, and Emperor Shundi too came to regard him with suspicion.

sentences.zh: 廷臣嘩言擴廓受命平江、淮，乃西攻關中，今罷兵不奉詔，跋扈有狀。

translations.literal: Court ministers clamored that Kuokuotiemuer had been ordered to pacify the Yangzi and Huai yet had attacked Guanzhong in the west; now he would not cease fighting or obey the edict—his overbearing conduct was evident.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers clamored that Kuokuotiemuer had been charged with pacifying the south yet had turned west to fight in Guanzhong, and now refused to halt his private war—his defiance was plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 及貊高奏至，順帝乃削擴廓太傅、中書左丞相，令以河南王就食邑汝南，分其軍隸諸將；

translations.literal: When Mo Gao's memorial arrived, Emperor Shundi then stripped Kuokuotiemuer of the offices of Grand Tutor and left chief councillor of the Central Secretariat, ordered him as Prince of Henan to take his fief at Runan, and divided his army among the various generals;
translations.idiomatic: When Mo Gao's memorial reached the court, Emperor Shundi stripped Kuokuotiemuer of his posts as grand tutor and left chief councillor, ordered him as Prince of Henan to retire to his fief at Runan, and broke up his army among the other commanders;

sentences.zh: 而以貊高知樞密院事兼平章，總河北軍，賜其軍號「忠義功臣」。

translations.literal: and made Mo Gao commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrent grand councillor, in overall command of the Hebei army, bestowing on his troops the title Loyal and Righteous Meritorious Warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Gao was made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and grand councillor, given overall command of the Hebei armies, and his troops were honored with the title Loyal and Righteous Meritorious Warriors.

sentences.zh: 太子開撫軍院于京師，總制天下兵馬，專備擴廓。

translations.literal: The crown prince opened the Pacification Army Bureau in the capital to control all troops and horses under heaven, devoted solely to guarding against Kuokuotiemuer.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince established the Pacification Army Bureau in the capital to command all military forces, aimed specifically at countering Kuokuotiemuer.

sentences.zh: 擴廓既受詔，退軍澤州，其部將關保亦歸於朝。

translations.literal: After Kuokuotiemuer had received the edict, he withdrew the army to Zezhou; his subordinate general Guan Bao also submitted to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemuer obeyed the edict and withdrew to Zezhou; his subordinate Guan Bao also submitted to the court.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知擴廓勢孤，乃詔李思齊等東出關，與貊高合攻擴廓，而令關保以兵戍太原。

translations.literal: The court, knowing Kuokuotiemuer's position was isolated, then ordered Li Siqi and others east out of the passes to join Mo Gao in attacking Kuokuotiemuer, and ordered Guan Bao to garrison Taiyuan with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Kuokuotiemuer isolated, the court ordered Li Siqi and the others east through the passes to join Mo Gao in attacking him, while Guan Bao was told to garrison Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 擴廓憤甚，引軍據太原，盡殺朝廷所置官吏。

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemuer was greatly enraged; he led troops to seize Taiyuan and killed all officials the court had appointed there.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Kuokuotiemuer seized Taiyuan and executed every official the court had posted there.

sentences.zh: 於是順帝下詔盡削擴廓官爵，令諸軍四面討之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Emperor Shundi issued an edict stripping Kuokuotiemuer of all offices and titles, and ordered all armies to attack him from four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shundi then stripped him of every rank and title and ordered armies on all sides to converge against him.

sentences.zh: 是時明兵已下山東，收大樑。

translations.literal: At that time Ming troops had already descended into Shandong and recovered Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: By then Ming forces had swept into Shandong and retaken Daliang (Kaifeng).

sentences.zh: 梁王阿魯溫，察罕父也，以河南降。

translations.literal: Prince of Liang Aruwen—Chaghan's father—surrendered Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Aruwen, Prince of Liang—Chaghan Temur's father—surrendered Henan to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 脫因帖木兒敗走，餘皆望風降遁，無一人抗者。

translations.literal: Tuoyintiemuer was defeated and fled; the rest all surrendered or fled at sight of the wind—no one resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoyintiemuer was routed and fled; the rest surrendered or scattered at the first approach of Ming troops—not one stood to fight.

sentences.zh: 既迫潼關，思齊等倉皇解兵西歸，而貊高、關保皆為擴廓所擒殺。

translations.literal: When they had pressed upon Tong Pass, Siqi and the others in panic disbanded the army and returned west; Mo Gao and Guan Bao were both captured and killed by Kuokuotiemuer.
translations.idiomatic: As Ming forces pressed Tong Pass, Li Siqi and his allies hastily disbanded and fled west; Mo Gao and Guan Bao were both captured and executed by Kuokuotiemuer.

sentences.zh: 順帝大恐，下詔歸罪於太子，罷撫軍院，悉復擴廓官，令與思齊等分道南討。

translations.literal: Emperor Shundi was greatly afraid; he issued an edict placing blame on the crown prince, abolished the Pacification Army Bureau, fully restored Kuokuotiemuer's offices, and ordered him and Siqi and others to campaign south by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Emperor Shundi blamed the crown prince, abolished the Pacification Army Bureau, restored all of Kuokuotiemuer's offices, and ordered him and Li Siqi to march south by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 詔下一月，明兵已逼大都，順帝北走。

translations.literal: One month after the edict was issued, Ming troops had already pressed upon Dadu; Emperor Shundi fled north.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month of the edict, Ming armies were at the gates of Dadu and Emperor Shundi fled north.

sentences.zh: 擴廓入援不及，大都遂陷，距察罕死時僅六年雲。

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemuer could not arrive in time to relieve the capital; Dadu then fell—it was only six years from Chaghan's death.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemuer could not reach the capital in time; Dadu fell—only six years after Chaghan Temur's death.

sentences.zh: 明兵已定元都，將軍湯和等自澤州徇山西。

translations.literal: After Ming troops had secured the Yuan capital, Generals Tang He and others advanced from Zezhou into Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Ming had secured the former Yuan capital, Generals Tang He and others advanced from Zezhou into Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 擴廓遣將禦之，戰于韓店，明師大敗。

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemuer sent generals to resist them; they fought at Handian and the Ming army suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemuer sent his generals to meet them; at Handian the Ming army was routed.

sentences.zh: 會順帝自開平命擴廓復大都，擴廓乃北出雁門，將由保安徑居庸以攻北平。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Shundi from Kaiping ordered Kuokuotiemuer to recover Dadu; Kuokuotiemuer then went north out of Yanmen, intending to pass through Bao'an and directly via Juyong to attack Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shundi, now at Kaiping (Shangdu), ordered Kuokuotiemuer to retake Dadu; he marched north through Yanmen Pass, planning to strike Beiping via Bao'an and Juyong Pass.

sentences.zh: 徐達、常遇春乘虛搗太原，擴廓還救。

translations.literal: Xu Da and Chang Yuchun took advantage of the opening to strike at Taiyuan; Kuokuotiemuer turned back to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da and Chang Yuchun exploited the opening to strike at Taiyuan, forcing Kuokuotiemuer to turn back to its relief.

sentences.zh: 部將豁鼻馬潛約降於明。

translations.literal: His subordinate general Huobima secretly agreed to surrender to the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate Huobima secretly negotiated a surrender to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 明兵夜劫營，營中驚潰。

translations.literal: Ming troops raided the camp by night; the camp panicked and collapsed in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Ming troops raided the camp by night, and his army broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 擴廓倉卒以十八騎北走，明兵遂西入關。

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemuer in haste fled north with eighteen horsemen; Ming troops then entered the passes to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemuer fled north with only eighteen horsemen; the Ming army then pushed west through the passes.

sentences.zh: 思齊以臨洮降。

translations.literal: Siqi surrendered at Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siqi surrendered at Lintao.

sentences.zh: 思道走寧夏，其弟良臣以慶陽降，既而復叛，明兵破誅之。

translations.literal: Sidao fled to Ningxia; his younger brother Liangchen surrendered at Qingyang, then rebelled again; Ming troops defeated and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sidao fled to Ningxia; his brother Liangchen surrendered at Qingyang, rebelled again, and was defeated and executed by Ming forces.

sentences.zh: 於是元臣皆入於明，唯擴廓擁兵塞上，西北邊苦之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuan ministers all entered Ming service; only Kuokuotiemuer held troops on the frontier passes, and the northwestern border suffered from him.
translations.idiomatic: One by one the Yuan commanders submitted to the Ming; only Kuokuotiemuer held the northern passes with his army, and the northwestern frontier groaned under his raids.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，太祖命大將軍徐達總大兵出西安，搗定西。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, the founding emperor ordered Grand General Xu Da to command a great army out from Xi'an and strike into Dingxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 (1370), the founding emperor ordered Grand General Xu Da to lead a major force from Xi'an against Dingxi.

sentences.zh: 擴廓方圍蘭州，趨赴之。

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemuer was just then besieging Lanzhou and hurried to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemuer was besieging Lanzhou and rushed to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 戰于沈兒峪，大敗，盡亡其眾，獨與妻子數人北走，至黃河，得流木以渡，遂奔和林。

translations.literal: They fought at Shen'er Valley; he suffered a great defeat, lost all his followers, and fled north alone with his wife and a few others; reaching the Yellow River, he found floating timber to cross and then fled to Karakorum.
translations.idiomatic: At Shen'er Valley he was crushingly defeated and lost his entire force; he fled north with only his wife and a handful of companions, crossed the Yellow River on driftwood, and made for Karakorum.

sentences.zh: 時順帝崩，太子嗣立，復任以國事。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Shundi had died; the crown prince succeeded and again entrusted him with state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shundi had by then died; the crown prince succeeded and again put him in charge of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 逾年，太祖復遣大將軍徐達、左副將軍李文忠、征西將軍馮勝將十五萬眾，分道出塞取擴廓。

translations.literal: After more than a year, the founding emperor again sent Grand General Xu Da, Left Deputy General Li Wenzhong, and Western Campaign General Feng Sheng with one hundred fifty thousand men by separate routes beyond the passes to take Kuokuotiemuer.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the founding emperor sent Grand General Xu Da, Left Deputy General Li Wenzhong, and Western Campaign General Feng Sheng with 150,000 men by separate routes beyond the frontier to capture Kuokuotiemuer.

sentences.zh: 大將軍至嶺北，與擴廓遇，大敗，死者數萬人。

translations.literal: The grand general reached Lingbei and encountered Kuokuotiemuer; he suffered a great defeat, and tens of thousands died.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da reached Lingbei, met Kuokuotiemuer in battle, and was routed with tens of thousands dead.

sentences.zh: 劉基嘗言于太祖曰：「擴廓未可輕也。

translations.literal: Liu Ji had once said to the founding emperor: Kuokuotiemuer must not be taken lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji had once warned the founding emperor: "Kuokuotiemuer is not to be underestimated."

sentences.zh: 」至是帝思其言，謂晉王曰：「吾用兵未嘗敗北。

translations.literal: At this the emperor recalled his words and said to the Prince of Jin: I have never been defeated in the north in my use of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor recalled his warning and told the Prince of Jin: "I have never before suffered a defeat in the north."

sentences.zh: 今諸將自請深入，敗于和林，輕信無謀，致多殺士卒，不可不戒。

translations.literal: Now the generals asked on their own to advance deep; they were defeated at Karakorum—credulous and without strategy, causing many soldiers to be killed; this must not go unheeded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my generals pressed for a deep advance on their own initiative and were beaten at Karakorum—rash and ill-advised, costing the lives of countless soldiers. This must be a lesson to us all."

sentences.zh: 」明年，擴廓復攻雁門，命諸將嚴為之備，自是明兵希出塞矣。

translations.literal: The next year Kuokuotiemuer again attacked Yanmen; he ordered the generals to guard it strictly; from then on Ming troops rarely went beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Kuokuotiemuer attacked Yanmen Pass again; the emperor ordered his generals to hold the frontier strictly, and thereafter Ming armies rarely ventured beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 其後，擴廓從其主徙金山，卒于哈剌那海之衙庭，其妻毛氏亦自經死，蓋洪武八年也。

translations.literal: Thereafter Kuokuotiemuer followed his lord in moving to Jinshan; he died at the yamen of Karanai; his wife Lady Mao also hanged herself—it was in the eighth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kuokuotiemuer followed his sovereign to Jinshan; he died at the yamen of Karanai, and his wife Lady Mao hanged herself as well—this was in Hongwu year 8 (1375).

sentences.zh: 初，察罕破山東，江、淮震動。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chaghan had broken Shandong, the Yangzi and Huai were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaghan Temur had conquered Shandong, the Yangzi and Huai regions were thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣使通好。

translations.literal: The founding emperor sent envoys to open friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming founder sent envoys to propose an alliance.

sentences.zh: 元遣戶部尚書張昶、郎中馬合謀浮海如江東，授太祖榮祿大夫、江西等處行中書省平章政事，賜以龍衣禦酒。

translations.literal: The Yuan sent Minister of Revenue Zhang Chang and Director Ma Hemou by sea to Jiangdong, appointing the founding emperor Honored Minister and Grand Councillor of the Jiangxi Regional Secretariat, and bestowing dragon robes and imperial wine.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan court sent Minister of Revenue Zhang Chang and Director Ma Hemou by sea to Jiangdong, offering the founder the title of honored minister and grand councillor of the Jiangxi regional secretariat, along with dragon robes and imperial wine.

sentences.zh: 甫至而察罕被刺，太祖遂不受，殺馬合謀，以張昶才，留官之。

translations.literal: They had just arrived when Chaghan was assassinated; the founding emperor then did not accept the appointment, killed Ma Hemou, and because of Zhang Chang's talent kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: They had scarcely arrived when Chaghan Temur was assassinated; the founder refused the Yuan titles, executed Ma Hemou, but kept Zhang Chang in office for his ability.

sentences.zh: 及擴廓視師河南，太祖乃復遣使通好，擴廓輒留使者不遣。

translations.literal: When Kuokuotiemuer took command in Henan, the founding emperor again sent envoys to open friendly relations; Kuokuotiemuer at once detained the envoys and would not send them back.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuokuotiemuer took command in Henan, the founder again sent envoys seeking peace; Kuokuotiemuer detained them and refused to let them return.

sentences.zh: 凡七致書，皆不答。

translations.literal: In all he sent seven letters; none received a reply.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote seven times in all; Kuokuotiemuer never replied.

sentences.zh: 既出塞，復遣人招諭，亦不應。

translations.literal: After he had gone beyond the passes, he again sent men to summon and instruct him; still no response.
translations.idiomatic: After Kuokuotiemuer withdrew beyond the frontier, the founder sent envoys again to win him over; still he would not respond.

sentences.zh: 最後使李思齊往。

translations.literal: Finally he sent Li Siqi to go.
translations.idiomatic: Finally the founder sent Li Siqi as envoy.

sentences.zh: 始至，則待以禮。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, he was received with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival Kuokuotiemuer received him with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 尋使騎士送歸，至塞下，辭曰：「主帥有命，請公留一物為別。

translations.literal: Shortly he sent horsemen to escort him back; at the frontier they took leave, saying: The commander has ordered—please leave something with us as a parting token.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he sent horsemen to escort him home; at the frontier they said: "Our commander bids you leave something behind as a keepsake."

sentences.zh: 」思齊曰：「吾遠來無所齎。

translations.literal: Siqi said: I have come from afar and brought nothing with me.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siqi said: "I have come from far away and brought nothing with me."

sentences.zh: 」騎士曰：「願得公一臂。

translations.literal: The horsemen said: We wish to have one of your arms.
translations.idiomatic: The horsemen said: "We would like one of your arms."

sentences.zh: 」思齊知不免，遂斷與之。

translations.literal: Siqi knew he could not escape; he then cut it off and gave it to them.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not refuse, Li Siqi cut off his arm and gave it to them.

sentences.zh: 還，未幾死。

translations.literal: He returned; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home and died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 太祖以是心敬擴廓。

translations.literal: Because of this the founding emperor inwardly respected Kuokuotiemuer.
translations.idiomatic: From this the founding emperor came to respect Kuokuotiemuer in his heart.

sentences.zh: 一日，大會諸將，問曰：「天下奇男子誰也？

translations.literal: One day he held a great assembly of generals and asked: Who in the realm is the extraordinary man?
translations.idiomatic: One day at a grand assembly of his generals he asked: "Who is the most remarkable man under heaven?"

sentences.zh: 」皆對曰：「常遇春將不過萬人，橫行無敵，真奇男子。

translations.literal: All answered: Chang Yuchun commands no more than ten thousand men yet marches unopposed—he is truly the extraordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: All answered: "Chang Yuchun—he commands fewer than ten thousand men yet marches unopposed. He is the true extraordinary man."

sentences.zh: 」太祖笑曰：「遇春雖人傑，吾得而臣之。

translations.literal: The founding emperor laughed and said: Though Yuchun is a great man, I was able to make him my subject.
translations.idiomatic: The founder laughed and said: "Chang Yuchun is a great man, yet I was able to win him to my service."

sentences.zh: 吾不能臣王保保，其人奇男子也。

translations.literal: I could not make Wang Baobao my subject—he is the extraordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: But I could not win Wang Baobao—he is the true extraordinary man."

sentences.zh: 」竟冊其妹為秦王妃。

translations.literal: In the end he enfeoffed Baobao's younger sister as Princess Consort of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he enfeoffed Kuokuotiemuer's sister as consort to the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 張昶仕明，累官中書省參知政事，有才辨，明習故事，裁決如流，甚見信任。

translations.literal: Zhang Chang served the Ming, rose through offices to Vice Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat; he had talent and eloquence, was clear on precedents, decided cases like flowing water, and was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang entered Ming service and rose to vice grand councillor of the Central Secretariat; gifted and eloquent, thoroughly versed in precedent, he decided cases with ease and enjoyed the founder's full trust.

sentences.zh: 自以故元臣，心嘗戀戀。

translations.literal: Regarding himself as a former Yuan minister, his heart often yearned toward the north.
translations.idiomatic: As a former Yuan official, his heart still yearned toward his old masters.

sentences.zh: 會太祖縱降人北還，昶附私書訪其子存亡。

translations.literal: It happened that the founding emperor allowed surrendered men to return north; Chang attached a private letter inquiring whether his son was alive or dead.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder allowed surrendered northerners to return home, Zhang attached a private letter asking after his son's welfare.

sentences.zh: 楊憲得書稿以聞，下吏按問。

translations.literal: Yang Xian obtained the draft of the letter and reported it; officials were sent to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xian obtained the draft and reported it; officials were ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 昶大書牘背曰：「身在江南，心思塞北。

translations.literal: Chang wrote large characters on the back of the document, saying: Though my body is in the south of the Yangzi, my thoughts are on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang wrote boldly on the back of the document: "My body is in the south, but my heart is on the northern frontier."

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃殺之。

translations.literal: The founding emperor then had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: The founder then had him executed.

sentences.zh: 而擴廓幕下士不屈節縱出塞者，有蔡子英。

translations.literal: Among Kuokuotiemuer's staff who would not bend their integrity and were allowed to go beyond the passes was Cai Ziying.
translations.idiomatic: Among Kuokuotiemuer's retainers who refused to compromise and were eventually allowed to leave the frontier was Cai Ziying.

sentences.zh: 蔡子英

translations.literal: Cai Ziying.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ziying

sentences.zh: 子英，永寧人，元至正中進士。

translations.literal: Ziying was a man of Yongning; he passed the civil examination in the Zhizheng era of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ziying was from Yongning and had passed the civil examinations in the Zhizheng era.

sentences.zh: 察罕開府河南，辟參軍事，累薦至行省參政。

translations.literal: When Chaghan opened a headquarters in Henan, he recruited him as military aide; through repeated recommendations he rose to provincial vice administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaghan Temur established his headquarters in Henan, he recruited Ziying as a military aide; through repeated recommendations he rose to provincial vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 元亡，從擴廓走定西。

translations.literal: When the Yuan fell, he followed Kuokuotiemuer in flight to Dingxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan dynasty fell, he followed Kuokuotiemuer west to Dingxi.

sentences.zh: 明兵克定西，擴廓軍敗，子英單騎走關中，亡入南山。

translations.literal: Ming troops captured Dingxi; Kuokuotiemuer's army was defeated; Ziying fled alone on horseback into Guanzhong and hid in the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming forces took Dingxi and Kuokuotiemuer's army was routed, Ziying fled alone into Guanzhong and hid in the Qinling mountains.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞其名，使人繪形求得之，傳詣京師。

translations.literal: The founding emperor heard his name and sent men to paint his likeness and seek him out; he was conveyed to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The founder, hearing of him, had his portrait painted and sent men to hunt him down; he was brought to the capital under escort.

sentences.zh: 至江濱，亡去，變姓名，賃舂。

translations.literal: When he reached the riverbank he fled, changed his name, and hired himself out to pound grain.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yangzi he escaped, assumed a false name, and hired himself out as a mill hand.

sentences.zh: 久之，復被獲。

translations.literal: After a long time he was captured again.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was captured again.

sentences.zh: 械過洛陽，見湯和，長揖不拜。

translations.literal: In fetters he passed through Luoyang; seeing Tang He, he made a long bow but would not prostrate himself.
translations.idiomatic: In chains he passed through Luoyang; meeting Tang He, he bowed from the waist but refused to kneel.

sentences.zh: 抑之跪，不肯。

translations.literal: They forced him to kneel; he would not.
translations.idiomatic: They forced him to his knees; he would not comply.

sentences.zh: 和怒，爇火焚其須，不動。

translations.literal: He grew angry and lit a fire to burn his beard; he did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Tang He in anger set fire to his beard; Ziying did not flinch.

sentences.zh: 其妻適在洛，請與相見，子英避不肯見。

translations.literal: His wife happened to be in Luoyang and asked to see him; Ziying avoided her and would not meet.
translations.idiomatic: His wife happened to be in Luoyang and asked to see him; he refused to meet her.

sentences.zh: 至京，太祖命脫械以禮遇之，授以官，不受。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, the founding emperor ordered his fetters removed and received him with ceremony, offered him office; he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital the founder had his chains removed, received him with courtesy, and offered him office; he refused.

sentences.zh: 退而上書曰：「陛下乘時應運，削平群雄，薄海內外，莫不賓貢。

translations.literal: He withdrew and submitted a memorial, saying: Your Majesty, riding the times and responding to destiny, has cut down the contending warlords; within and beyond the seas none fail to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty, seizing heaven's mandate, has crushed the rival warlords; within the four seas and beyond, all now offer tribute."

sentences.zh: 臣鼎魚漏網，假息南山。

translations.literal: Your subject, a fish in the cauldron who slipped the net, borrowed rest in the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: I was a fish that slipped the cauldron's net and took refuge in the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 曩者見獲，復得脫亡。

translations.literal: Formerly when captured, I again escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Once captured, I escaped again.

sentences.zh: 七年之久，重煩有司追跡。

translations.literal: For seven years officials were again troubled to pursue me.
translations.idiomatic: For seven years your officials were again put to the trouble of hunting me down.

sentences.zh: 而陛下以萬乘之尊，全匹夫之節，不降天誅，反療其疾，易冠裳，賜酒饌，授以官爵，陛下之量包乎天地矣。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty, with the dignity of the ten-thousand-chariot ruler, preserved a commoner's integrity, did not send down heaven's punishment but instead treated my illness, changed my cap and robes, bestowed wine and food, and granted rank and salary—Your Majesty's magnanimity embraces heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty, sovereign of ten thousand chariots, honored a commoner's integrity—sparing me heaven's punishment, tending my illness, clothing me anew, feasting me, and offering rank and emolument. Your magnanimity embraces heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 臣感恩無極，非不欲自竭犬馬，但名義所存，不敢輒渝初志。

translations.literal: Your subject's gratitude is boundless; it is not that I do not wish to exhaust myself like a dog or horse, but where righteousness and reputation stand, I dare not lightly betray my original resolve.
translations.idiomatic: My gratitude is boundless, and it is not that I would not serve you with my life—but where duty and honor stand, I dare not betray my first loyalty.

sentences.zh: 自惟身本韋布，智識淺陋，過蒙主將知薦，仕至七命，躍馬食肉十有五年，愧無尺寸以報國士之遇。

translations.literal: Reflecting that I was originally but coarse cloth, shallow in wisdom and knowledge, yet overly favored by my commander who knew and recommended me, I served to the seventh rank, rode horses and ate meat for fifteen years, yet am ashamed to have not a span's measure to repay the state's scholar's treatment of me.
translations.idiomatic: I was but a commoner, shallow in learning, yet my commander favored me and raised me to the seventh rank; for fifteen years I rode at his side—yet I have not a span's worth of merit to repay his trust.

sentences.zh: 及國家破亡，又復失節，何面目見天下士。

translations.literal: When the state was destroyed I again lost my integrity—what face have I to meet the scholars under heaven?
translations.idiomatic: When the state fell I failed in my duty again—what face have I to show the world's scholars?

sentences.zh: 管子曰：『禮義廉恥，國之四維。

translations.literal: Guanzi said: Propriety, righteousness, integrity, and shame are the four bonds of a state.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzi said: 'Propriety, righteousness, integrity, and shame are the four bonds of a state.'

sentences.zh: 』今陛下創業垂統，正當挈持大經大法，垂示子孫臣民。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is founding the enterprise and handing down the succession; you should just then uphold the great canon and great law and display it to descendants and subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is founding a dynasty to last ten thousand generations; you should uphold the great principles of governance and display them to your heirs and your people.

sentences.zh: 奈何欲以無禮義、寡廉恥之俘囚，廁諸維新之朝、賢士大夫之列哉！

translations.literal: How can you wish to place a captive without propriety and righteousness, bereft of integrity and shame, among the ranks of the renewing court's worthy scholars and officials!
translations.idiomatic: How can you place a captive devoid of propriety, righteousness, integrity, and shame among the worthy scholars and officials of your renewing court!

sentences.zh: 臣日夜思維，咎往昔之不死，至於今日，分宜自裁。

translations.literal: Your subject day and night reflects and blames himself that in the past he did not die; coming to today, by rights he should take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night I blame myself that I did not die when I should have; by rights I ought to take my own life today.

sentences.zh: 陛下待臣以恩禮，臣固不敢賣死立名，亦不敢偷生苟祿。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has treated your subject with favor and ceremony; your subject truly dares not sell death to make a name, nor dare cling to life for a salary.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has treated me with grace; I would not court death for fame, nor cling to life for a salary.

sentences.zh: 若察臣之愚，全臣之志，禁錮海南，畢其餘命，則雖死之日，猶生之年。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty perceives your subject's folly and fulfills your subject's resolve, imprisoning him in Hainan to finish his remaining life, then even on the day of death it would be as the years of life.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty sees my folly and honors my resolve—imprison me in Hainan for the rest of my days—then even in death I would count myself among the living.

sentences.zh: 或王蠋閉戶以自縊，李芾闔門以自屠，彼非惡榮利而樂死亡，顧義之所在，雖湯鑊有不得避也。

translations.literal: Some, like Wang Shu who closed his door and hanged himself, or Li Fu who shut his household and slaughtered themselves—they did not hate glory and profit and love death, but where righteousness lay, even boiling cauldron they could not avoid.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu barred his door and hanged himself; Li Fu shut his household and perished with his kin—they did not despise life and court death, but where duty lay, even the boiling cauldron could not be avoided.

sentences.zh: 渺焉之軀，上愧古人，死有餘恨，惟陛下裁察。

translations.literal: This slight body shames the ancients above; in death there is surplus regret—only Your Majesty's judgment is sought.
translations.idiomatic: This slight frame shames the ancients; in death I would still have regrets—only Your Majesty's judgment can decide.

sentences.zh: 」帝覽其書，益重之，館之儀曹。

translations.literal: The emperor read his memorial and esteemed him all the more, lodging him in the Ceremonies Office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read his memorial and esteemed him all the more, lodging him in the Ceremonies Office.

sentences.zh: 忽一夜大哭不止。

translations.literal: Suddenly one night he wept without cease.
translations.idiomatic: One night he suddenly wept without stopping.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，曰：「無他，思舊君耳。

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, he said: Nothing else—I am thinking of my former lord, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said: "Nothing else—I am thinking of my former sovereign, that is all."

sentences.zh: 」帝知不可奪，洪武九年十二月命有司送出塞，令從故主于和林。

translations.literal: The emperor knew he could not be turned; in the twelfth month of the ninth year of Hongwu he ordered officials to send him beyond the passes and let him follow his former lord at Karakorum.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that his loyalty could not be swayed, in the twelfth month of Hongwu year 9 (1376) the emperor ordered officials to send him beyond the frontier to join his former master at Karakorum.

sentences.zh: 陳友定附 伯顏子中 等

translations.literal: Chen Youding, with appended biography: Bayan Zizhong, et al.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youding (with appended biography of Bayan Zizhong and others)

sentences.zh: 陳友定，一名有定，字安國，福清人，徙居汀之清流。

translations.literal: Chen Youding, also named Youding, style Anguo, was a man of Fuqing who moved to Qingliu in Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youding, also known as Youding, style name Anguo, was from Fuqing and later moved to Qingliu in Ting Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世業農。

translations.literal: His family for generations practiced farming.
translations.idiomatic: His family had farmed for generations.

sentences.zh: 為人沉勇，喜遊俠。

translations.literal: As a man he was deep and brave, fond of roaming as a knight-errant.
translations.idiomatic: He was resolute and brave, and fond of the wandering life of a knight-errant.

sentences.zh: 鄉里皆畏服。

translations.literal: The village and countryside all feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: The whole countryside feared and obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 至正中，汀州府判蔡公安至清流募民兵討賊，友定應募。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng era, the Tingzhou prefectural judge Cai Gong'an came to Qingliu to recruit militia to suppress bandits; Youding answered the call.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhizheng era, Prefectural Judge Cai Gong'an of Tingzhou came to Qingliu to raise militia against bandits; Youding enlisted.

sentences.zh: 公安與語，奇之，使掌所募兵，署為黃土砦巡檢。

translations.literal: Gong'an spoke with him, found him extraordinary, put him in charge of the recruited troops, and appointed him inspector of Huangtu Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Cai was impressed in conversation and put him in command of the militia, appointing him inspector of Huangtu Stockade.

sentences.zh: 以討平諸山寨功，遷清流縣尹。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying the various mountain stockades, he was transferred to magistrate of Qingliu County.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying the mountain strongholds he was promoted to magistrate of Qingliu County.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒遣其將鄧克明等陷汀、邵，略杉關。

translations.literal: Chen Youliang sent his generals Deng Keming and others to seize Ting and Shao and overrun Shan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youliang sent his generals Deng Keming and others to take Ting and Shao and overrun Shan Pass.

sentences.zh: 行省授友定汀州路總管禦之。

translations.literal: The provincial administration appointed Youding circuit intendant of Tingzhou to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial administration appointed Youding circuit intendant of Tingzhou to resist them.

sentences.zh: 戰于黃土，大捷，走克明。

translations.literal: They fought at Huangtu and won a great victory, driving off Keming.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangtu he won a great victory and drove off Deng Keming.

sentences.zh: 逾年，克明復取汀州，急攻建寧。

translations.literal: After more than a year Keming again took Tingzhou and pressed the attack on Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Deng Keming retook Tingzhou and pressed the attack on Jianning.

sentences.zh: 守將完者帖木兒檄友定入援，連破賊，悉復所失郡縣。

translations.literal: The defending general Wanzh Temur summoned Youding to relieve him; he repeatedly defeated the bandits and fully recovered the lost prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: The defender Wanzh Temur summoned Youding to his aid; he repeatedly routed the rebels and recovered every lost prefecture and county.

sentences.zh: 行省上其功第一，進參知政事。

translations.literal: The provincial administration reported his merit as foremost; he was advanced to vice administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The province ranked his merit first and promoted him to vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 已，置分省于延平，以友定為平章，於是友定盡有福建八郡之地。

translations.literal: Thereafter a branch secretariat was established at Yanping with Youding as grand councillor; thus Youding came to hold all eight prefectures of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: A branch secretariat was then set up at Yanping with Youding as grand councillor, and he came to control all eight prefectures of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 友定以農家子起傭伍，目不知書。

translations.literal: Youding rose from hired labor as a farmer's son and could not read by sight.
translations.idiomatic: Youding had risen from hired farm labor and could not read.

sentences.zh: 及據八郡，數招致文學知名士，如閩縣鄭定、廬州王翰之屬，留置幕下。

translations.literal: When he held the eight prefectures, he repeatedly summoned renowned literary scholars such as Zheng Ding of Min County and Wang Han of Luzhou, keeping them in his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the eight prefectures, he repeatedly recruited renowned scholars such as Zheng Ding of Min County and Wang Han of Luzhou to his staff.

sentences.zh: 粗涉文史，習為五字小詩，皆有意理。

translations.literal: He roughly touched on letters and history, practiced five-character short poems—all had intentional meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He picked up some learning and composed five-character verses that showed genuine thought.

sentences.zh: 然頗任威福，所屬違令者輒承制誅竄不絕。

translations.literal: Yet he quite wielded authority and favor; those under him who disobeyed orders were continually executed or banished on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he ruled with arbitrary power; subordinates who disobeyed were continually executed or banished on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 漳州守將羅良不平，以書責之曰：「郡縣者，國家之土地。

translations.literal: The Zhangzhou defending general Luo Liang was displeased and rebuked him in a letter, saying: Prefectures and counties are the state's lands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzhou's defender Luo Liang took offense and wrote to rebuke him: "Prefectures and counties are the state's lands.

sentences.zh: 官司者，人主之臣役。

translations.literal: Officials are the sovereign's servants.
translations.idiomatic: Officials are the sovereign's servants.

sentences.zh: 而廥廩者，朝廷之外府也。

translations.literal: Granaries are the outer storehouses of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries are the court's outer storehouses.

sentences.zh: 今足下視郡縣如室家，驅官僚如圉僕，擅廥廩如私藏，名雖報國，實有鷹揚跋扈之心。

translations.literal: Now you regard prefectures and counties as your household, drive officials like stable servants, monopolize granaries as private stores—though your name is serving the state, in truth you have the heart of an eagle soaring in insolence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you treat prefectures as your private household, drive officials like stable boys, and hoard grain as your own treasure—though you claim to serve the state, in truth you harbor the heart of a usurper."

sentences.zh: 不知足下欲為郭子儀乎，抑為曹孟德乎？

translations.literal: I do not know whether you wish to be Guo Ziyi, or rather Cao Mengde?
translations.idiomatic: Do you mean to be another Guo Ziyi, or another Cao Cao?"

sentences.zh: 」友定怒，竟以兵誅良。

translations.literal: Youding was enraged and in the end used troops to execute Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Youding in fury sent troops to kill Luo Liang.

sentences.zh: 而福清宣慰使陳瑞孫、崇安令孔楷、建陽人詹翰拒友定不從，皆被殺。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Fuqing pacification commissioner Chen Ruisun, the Chong'an magistrate Kong Kai, and the Jianyang man Zhan Han refused Youding and would not submit—all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Fuqing pacification commissioner Chen Ruisun, Chong'an magistrate Kong Kai, and the Jianyang scholar Zhan Han, who refused to submit, were all killed.

sentences.zh: 於是友定威震八閩，然事元未嘗失臣節。

translations.literal: Thereupon Youding's might shook the eight Min regions, yet in serving the Yuan he never lost a minister's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Youding's power now awed all Fujian, yet in his service to the Yuan he never wavered in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 是時張士誠據浙西，方國珍據浙東，名為附元，歲漕粟大都輒不至。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Shicheng held western Zhejiang and Fang Guozhen held eastern Zhejiang; though nominally attached to the Yuan, their annual grain transport to Dadu often did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng held western Zhejiang and Fang Guozhen eastern Zhejiang; though nominally Yuan subjects, their annual grain shipments to Dadu rarely arrived.

sentences.zh: 而友定歲輸粟數十萬石，海道遼遠，至者嘗十三四。

translations.literal: But Youding each year transported several hundred thousand piculs of grain; the sea route was distant and far—of what was sent, only three or four tenths typically arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Youding, by contrast, shipped hundreds of thousands of piculs each year; the sea route was long and perilous, and only three or four tenths typically reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 順帝嘉之，下詔褒美。

translations.literal: Emperor Shundi commended this and issued an edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shundi commended him and issued an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 太祖既定婺州，與友定接境。

translations.literal: After the founding emperor had secured Wuzhou, he bordered on Youding.
translations.idiomatic: Once the founder had secured Wuzhou, his territory bordered Chen Youding's.

sentences.zh: 友定侵處州。

translations.literal: Youding invaded Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Youding invaded Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 參政胡深擊走之，遂下浦城，克松溪，獲友定將張子玉，與硃亮祖進攻建寧，破其二柵。

translations.literal: Vice Administrator Hu Shen drove him off, then descended on Pucheng, captured Songxi, seized Youding's general Zhang Ziyu, and with Zhu Liangzu advanced on Jianning and broke two of his stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Administrator Hu Shen drove him back, took Pucheng and Songxi, captured Youding's general Zhang Ziyu, and with Zhu Liangzu advanced on Jianning and broke two of his stockades.

sentences.zh: 友定遣阮德柔以兵四萬屯錦江，繞出深後，斷其歸路，而自帥牙將賴政等以銳師搏戰，德柔自後夾擊。

translations.literal: Youding sent Ruan Derou with forty thousand troops to encamp at Jinjiang, circling behind Shen to cut off his retreat, while he himself led the junior generals Lai Zheng and others with crack troops to grapple in battle; Derou struck from behind in a pincer.
translations.idiomatic: Youding sent Ruan Derou with forty thousand men to hold Jinjiang, swung around behind Hu Shen to cut his retreat, while he himself led his crack troops under Lai Zheng in the frontal fight and Derou struck from the rear.

sentences.zh: 深兵敗，被執死。

translations.literal: Shen's army was defeated; he was captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shen's army was defeated; he was captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 太祖既平方國珍，即發兵伐友定。

translations.literal: After the founding emperor had pacified Fang Guozhen, he at once sent troops to attack Youding.
translations.idiomatic: Once the founder had subdued Fang Guozhen, he immediately launched an offensive against Chen Youding.

sentences.zh: 將軍胡廷美、何文輝由江西趨杉關，湯和、廖永忠由明州海道取福州，李文忠由浦城取建寧，而別遣使至延平，招諭友定。

translations.literal: Generals Hu Tingmei and He Wenhui advanced from Jiangxi toward Shan Pass; Tang He and Liao Yongzhong took Fuzhou by the Mingzhou sea route; Li Wenzhong took Jianning from Pucheng; and separately envoys were sent to Yanping to summon and instruct Youding.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Hu Tingmei and He Wenhui advanced from Jiangxi toward Shan Pass; Tang He and Liao Yongzhong took the sea route from Mingzhou against Fuzhou; Li Wenzhong advanced from Pucheng on Jianning; and separate envoys were sent to Yanping to offer terms.

sentences.zh: 友定置酒大會諸將及賓客，殺明使者，瀝其血酒甕中，與眾酌飲之。

translations.literal: Youding set out wine and held a great assembly of generals and guests, killed the Ming envoys, drained their blood into the wine jar, and drank with the crowd from it.
translations.idiomatic: Youding held a great feast for his generals and guests, killed the Ming envoys, mixed their blood into the wine, and shared the cup with all present.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，誓於眾曰：「吾曹並受元厚恩，有不以死拒者，身磔，妻子戮。

translations.literal: When the wine was warm, he swore before the crowd: We all have received thick favor from the Yuan; whoever does not resist unto death—his body shall be dismembered, his wife and children executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was warm, he swore before them: "We have all received great favor from the Yuan; whoever does not resist to the death shall be dismembered, and his wife and children executed."

sentences.zh: 」遂往視福州，環城作壘。

translations.literal: He then went to inspect Fuzhou and built ramparts encircling the city.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Fuzhou and built ramparts around the city.

sentences.zh: 距壘五十步，輒築一台，嚴兵為拒守計。

translations.literal: Every fifty paces from the ramparts he built a tower, stationing strict troops for a plan of defense.
translations.idiomatic: Every fifty paces along the ramparts he built a watchtower and stationed troops for defense.

sentences.zh: 已而聞杉關破，急分軍為二，以一軍守福，而自帥一軍守延平，以相掎角。

translations.literal: Soon hearing that Shan Pass had fallen, he hastily divided the army in two—one army to hold Fu, he himself leading one army to hold Yanping, to support each other like pincers.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Shan Pass had fallen, he hastily split his forces—one corps to hold Fuzhou, he himself leading the other at Yanping in mutual support.

sentences.zh: 及湯和等舟師抵福之五虎門，平章曲出引兵逆戰敗，明兵緣南台蟻附登城。

translations.literal: When Tang He and others' fleet reached Fuzhou's Wuhu Gate, Grand Councillor Qu Chu led troops to meet them in battle and was defeated; Ming troops climbed the city along the South Terrace like ants.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang He's fleet reached Fuzhou's Wuhu Gate, Grand Councillor Qu Chu met them in battle and was defeated; Ming troops swarmed up the South Terrace wall like ants.

sentences.zh: 守將遁去，參政尹克仁、宣政使朵耳麻不屈死，僉院柏帖木兒積薪樓下，殺妻妾及二女，縱火自焚死。

translations.literal: The defending general fled; Vice Administrator Yin Keren and Pacification Commissioner Duo'erma died unyielding; Vice Commissioner Bo Temur piled firewood beneath a tower, killed his wives, concubines, and two daughters, and set fire to burn himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: The defender fled; Vice Administrator Yin Keren and Pacification Commissioner Duo'erma died defiant; Vice Commissioner Bo Temur piled firewood under a tower, killed his wives, concubines, and two daughters, and burned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 廷美克建甯，湯和進攻延平。

translations.literal: Tingmei captured Jianning; Tang He advanced the attack on Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Tingmei took Jianning while Tang He pressed the attack on Yanping.

sentences.zh: 友定欲以持久困之，諸將請出戰，不許。

translations.literal: Youding wished to wear them down by endurance; the generals asked to go out and fight; he would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Youding planned to wear them down in a siege; his generals repeatedly asked to give battle, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 數請不已，友定疑所部將叛，殺蕭院判。

translations.literal: They asked repeatedly without cease; Youding suspected his subordinate generals of rebellion and killed Vice Commissioner Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: When they pressed again and again, Youding suspected his officers of treason and executed Vice Commissioner Xiao.

sentences.zh: 軍士多出降者。

translations.literal: Many soldiers went out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers began surrendering in large numbers.

sentences.zh: 會軍器局災，城中礮聲震地，明師知有變，急攻城。

translations.literal: It happened that the Ordnance Bureau caught fire; cannon sounds in the city shook the earth; the Ming army knew something had changed and pressed the assault urgently.
translations.idiomatic: When the ordnance depot caught fire and cannon blasts shook the city, the Ming army sensed disorder and pressed the assault.

sentences.zh: 友定呼其屬訣曰：「大事已去，吾一死報國，諸君努力。

translations.literal: Youding called his subordinates to take leave, saying: The great affair is gone; I die once to repay the state—gentlemen, strive on.
translations.idiomatic: Youding took leave of his officers: "The cause is lost; I die once to repay the Yuan—do your utmost, all of you."

sentences.zh: 」因退入省堂，衣冠北面再拜，仰藥死。

translations.literal: He then withdrew into the provincial hall, dressed in cap and robes, bowed twice facing north, and took poison to die.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to the provincial hall, dressed in full regalia, bowed twice toward the north, and took poison.

sentences.zh: 所部爭開城門納明師。

translations.literal: His subordinates vied to open the city gates and admit the Ming army.
translations.idiomatic: His men rushed to open the gates and admit the Ming army.

sentences.zh: 師入，趨視之，猶未絕也。

translations.literal: The army entered and hurried to look at him; he was not yet dead.
translations.idiomatic: The troops entered and found him still alive.

sentences.zh: 舁出水東門，適天大雷雨，友定復蘇。

translations.literal: They carried him out the East Water Gate; just then heaven sent a great thunderstorm and Youding revived.
translations.idiomatic: They carried him out the East Water Gate; a great thunderstorm broke, and Youding revived.

sentences.zh: 械送京師。

translations.literal: In fetters he was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to the capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 入見，帝詰之。

translations.literal: He entered audience; the emperor interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: Brought before the emperor, he was interrogated.

sentences.zh: 友定曆聲曰：「國破家亡，死耳，尚何言。

translations.literal: Youding said in a harsh voice: The state is broken, the family destroyed—death is all; what more is there to say?
translations.idiomatic: Youding said harshly: "The state is fallen and my house destroyed—death is all that remains. What more is there to say?"

sentences.zh: 」遂並其子海殺之。

translations.literal: He then had him and his son Hai killed together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had him and his son Hai executed together.

sentences.zh: 海，一名宗海，工騎射，亦喜禮文士。

translations.literal: Hai, also named Zonghai, was skilled in mounted archery and also delighted in honoring literary scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Hai, also called Zonghai, was skilled in mounted archery and cultivated the company of scholars.

sentences.zh: 友定既被執，自將樂歸於軍門，至是從死。

translations.literal: After Youding had been captured, he himself led troops from Jiangle to surrender at the army gate; at this time he followed his father in death.
translations.idiomatic: After his father was captured, Hai had led troops from Jiangle to surrender at the Ming camp; now he died with his father.

sentences.zh: 元末所在盜起，民間起義兵保障鄉里，稱元帥者不可勝數，元輒因而官之。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan bandits rose everywhere; the people raised righteous militia to protect their villages; those calling themselves marshals were beyond counting, and the Yuan regularly enfeoffed them as officials.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan, rebels rose everywhere; local militias sprang up to defend their communities, and countless men styled themselves marshals—the Yuan court regularly enfeoffed them as officials.

sentences.zh: 其後或去為盜，或事元不終，惟友定父子死義，時人稱完節焉。

translations.literal: Afterward some turned to banditry, some served the Yuan without finishing their loyalty—only the father and son Youding died for righteousness; people of the time praised their complete integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Later many turned bandit or abandoned their Yuan allegiance—only the Youdings, father and son, died for their cause, and contemporaries praised their unbroken loyalty.

sentences.zh: 友定既死，興化、泉州皆望風納疑。

translations.literal: After Youding died, Xinghua and Quanzhou all submitted at sight of the Ming forces.
translations.idiomatic: After Youding's death, Xinghua and Quanzhou surrendered at the first approach of Ming troops.

sentences.zh: 獨漳州路達魯花赤迭裏彌實具公服，北面再拜，引斧斫印章，以佩刀剚喉而死。

translations.literal: Only the Zhangzhou circuit darughachi Dielimishi, in full official dress, bowed twice facing north, took an axe to chop the seal, and stabbed his throat with his belt dagger to die.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhangzhou's darughachi Dielimishi, in full official regalia, bowed twice toward the north, smashed the seal with an axe, and cut his own throat with his dagger.

sentences.zh: 時雲「閩有三忠」，謂友定、柏帖木兒、迭裏彌實也。

translations.literal: People at the time said there were three loyal ones in Min—meaning Youding, Bo Temur, and Dielimishi.
translations.idiomatic: People said Fujian had three loyal martyrs: Chen Youding, Bo Temur, and Dielimishi.

sentences.zh: 鄭定，字孟宣。

translations.literal: Zheng Ding, style Mengxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ding, style name Mengxuan.

sentences.zh: 好擊劍，為友定記室。

translations.literal: He was fond of swordplay and served as Youding's recorder.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of swordplay and served as Chen Youding's secretary.

sentences.zh: 及敗，浮海入交、廣間。

translations.literal: When defeated, he went by sea into Jiaozhi and Guang regions.
translations.idiomatic: When Youding fell, he fled by sea to Annam and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 久之，還居長樂。

translations.literal: After a long time he returned to dwell in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: After many years he returned to live in Changle.

sentences.zh: 洪武末，累官至國子助教。

translations.literal: By the end of Hongwu he had risen through offices to assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Hongwu reign he had risen to assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 王翰，字用文，仕元為潮州路總管。

translations.literal: Wang Han, style Yongwen, served the Yuan as circuit intendant of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han, style name Yongwen, had served the Yuan as circuit intendant of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 友定敗，為黃冠，棲永泰山中者十載。

translations.literal: When Youding was defeated, he became a Daoist priest and dwelt in Yongtai Mountain for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Youding fell, he became a Daoist recluse and lived on Yongtai Mountain for ten years.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞其賢，強起之，自刎死，有子偁知名。

translations.literal: The founding emperor heard of his worth and forcibly summoned him; he cut his own throat and died; he had a son Cheng who became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: The founder, hearing of his virtue, forcibly summoned him; Wang Han cut his own throat rather than serve; his son Cheng became well known.

sentences.zh: 為友定所辟者，又有伯顏子中。

translations.literal: Among those recruited by Youding was also Bayan Zizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Another man recruited by Chen Youding was Bayan Zizhong.

sentences.zh: 子中，其先西域人，後仕江西，因家焉。

translations.literal: Zizhong's ancestors were Western Region people; later they served in Jiangxi and made their home there.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhong's family were originally from the Western Regions; they later settled in Jiangxi after entering Yuan service.

sentences.zh: 子中明《春秋》，五舉有司不第，行省辟授東湖書院山長，遷建昌教授。

translations.literal: Zizhong was versed in the Spring and Autumn Annals; five times he presented himself to the civil examinations without passing; the provincial administration recruited him as head of Donghu Academy, then transferred him to professor at Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhong was expert in the Spring and Autumn Annals; he failed the civil examinations five times; the province appointed him head of Donghu Academy and later professor at Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 子中雖儒生，慷慨喜談兵。

translations.literal: Though Zizhong was a Confucian scholar, he was magnanimous and fond of discussing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Though a scholar, Zizhong was bold and fond of military talk.

sentences.zh: 江西盜起，授分省都事，使守贛州，而陳友諒兵已破贛。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Jiangxi, he was appointed branch secretariat director and sent to guard Ganzhou—but Chen Youliang's troops had already taken Gan.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels rose in Jiangxi, he was made branch secretariat director and sent to defend Ganzhou—but Chen Youliang's army had already taken it.

sentences.zh: 子中倉卒募吏民，與鬥城下，不勝，脫身間道走閩。

translations.literal: Zizhong in haste recruited clerks and people, fought beneath the city walls, was not victorious, and escaped by a secret route to Min.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhong hastily raised militia and fought below the walls but was defeated; he escaped by a secret route to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 陳友定素知之，辟授行省員外郎。

translations.literal: Chen Youding had long known him and recruited him as provincial secretariat vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youding, who had long known him, appointed him provincial secretariat vice director.

sentences.zh: 出奇計，以友定兵復建昌，浮海如元都獻捷。

translations.literal: He devised a stratagem by which Youding's troops recovered Jianchang; he went by sea to the Yuan capital to present the victory.
translations.idiomatic: He devised a stratagem by which Youding's troops retook Jianchang, then sailed to Dadu to report the victory.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he rose to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through promotion to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 持節發廣東何真兵救閩，至則真已降于廖永忠。

translations.literal: Bearing credentials he mobilized He Zhen's Guangdong troops to relieve Min; when he arrived, Zhen had already surrendered to Liao Yongzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing imperial credentials he mobilized He Zhen's Guangdong forces to relieve Fujian; when he arrived, He Zhen had already surrendered to Liao Yongzhong.

sentences.zh: 子中跳墜馬，折一足，致軍前。

translations.literal: Zizhong leaped and fell from his horse, breaking one leg; he was brought before the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhong fell from his horse and broke a leg; he was brought before the Ming army.

sentences.zh: 永忠欲脅降之，不屈。

translations.literal: Yongzhong wished to coerce him to surrender; he would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Yongzhong tried to force his surrender; he refused.

sentences.zh: 永忠義而舍之。

translations.literal: Yongzhong, moved by righteousness, released him.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his integrity, Liao Yongzhong let him go.

sentences.zh: 乃變姓名，冠黃冠，遊行江湖間。

translations.literal: He then changed his name, put on the Daoist cap, and wandered among the rivers and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: He changed his name, became a Daoist priest, and wandered the country.

sentences.zh: 太祖求之不得，簿錄其妻子，子中竟不出。

translations.literal: The founding emperor sought him but could not find him; he registered his wife and children in the records; Zizhong in the end did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: The founder hunted for him in vain and registered his wife and children; Zizhong never came forward.

sentences.zh: 嘗齎鴆自隨，久之事浸解，乃還鄉里。

translations.literal: He once carried poison with him; after a long time the affair gradually eased, and he returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: He carried poison with him always; as the hunt eased, he returned home.

sentences.zh: 洪武十二年詔郡縣舉元遺民。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongwu an edict ordered prefectures and counties to recommend surviving Yuan subjects.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 12 (1379) an edict ordered local officials to recommend surviving Yuan loyalists.

sentences.zh: 布政使沈立本密言子中於朝，以幣聘。

translations.literal: Provincial administration commissioner Shen Liben secretly reported Zizhong to the court, and gifts were sent to engage him.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Commissioner Shen Liben secretly recommended him to court, and envoys were sent with gifts to engage him.

sentences.zh: 使者至，子中太息曰：「死晚矣。

translations.literal: When the envoys arrived, Zizhong sighed deeply and said: I have died too late.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys arrived, Zizhong sighed: "I have lived too long."

sentences.zh: 」為歌七章，哭其祖父師友，飲鴆而死。

translations.literal: He composed seven songs, wept for his grandfather, teachers, and friends, and drank poison to die.
translations.idiomatic: He composed seven laments, mourned his grandfather, teachers, and friends, and drank poison.

sentences.zh: 當元亡時，守土臣仗節死者甚眾。

translations.literal: When the Yuan perished, territorial officials who upheld their integrity and died were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan fell, countless territorial officials died defending their posts.

sentences.zh: 明兵克太平，總管靳義赴水死。

translations.literal: When Ming troops took Taiping, Circuit Intendant Jin Yi went into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming forces took Taiping, Circuit Intendant Jin Yi drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 攻集慶，行台御史大夫福壽戰敗，嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Attacking Jiqing, Regional Censor-in-Chief Fushou was defeated in battle and clung to the city in a tight defense.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking Jiqing (Nanjing), Regional Censor-in-Chief Fushou was defeated and held the city in a desperate defense.

sentences.zh: 城破，猶督兵巷戰，坐伏龜樓指揮。

translations.literal: When the city fell he still directed troops in street fighting, seated in the Tortoise Tower directing operations.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he still directed street fighting from the Tortoise Tower.

sentences.zh: 左右或勸之遁，福壽叱而射之，遂死於兵。

translations.literal: Those beside him sometimes urged him to flee; Fushou rebuked them and shot at them, then died among the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When aides urged him to flee, Fushou rebuked them and shot at them, then died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 參政伯家奴、達魯花赤達尼達思等皆戰死。

translations.literal: Vice Administrator Bojianu, Darughachi Danidasi, and others all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Administrator Bojianu, Darughachi Danidasi, and others all fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 克鎮江，守將段武、平章定定戰死。

translations.literal: When Zhenjiang was taken, the defending general Duan Wu and Grand Councillor Dingding died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenjiang the defender Duan Wu and Grand Councillor Dingding died fighting.

sentences.zh: 克甯國，百戶張文貴殺妻妾自刎死。

translations.literal: When Ningguo was taken, Centurion Zhang Wengui killed his wives and concubines and cut his own throat to die.
translations.idiomatic: At Ningguo Centurion Zhang Wengui killed his wives and concubines and cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 克徽州，萬戶吳訥戰敗自殺。

translations.literal: When Huizhou was taken, Myriarch Wu Ne was defeated and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: At Huizhou Myriarch Wu Ne was defeated and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 克婺州，浙東廉訪使楊惠、婺州達魯花赤僧住戰死。

translations.literal: When Wuzhou was taken, Eastern Zhejiang Surveillance Commissioner Yang Hui and Wuzhou Darughachi Sengzhu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuzhou Surveillance Commissioner Yang Hui of eastern Zhejiang and Darughachi Sengzhu fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 克衢州，總管馬浩赴水死。

translations.literal: When Quzhou was taken, Circuit Intendant Ma Hao went into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Quzhou Circuit Intendant Ma Hao drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 石抺宜孫守處州，其母與弟厚孫先為明兵所獲，令為書招之。

translations.literal: Shi Moyisun defended Chuzhou; his mother and younger brother Housun were first captured by Ming troops, who ordered them to write a letter summoning him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Moyisun held Chuzhou; Ming forces captured his mother and brother Housun and forced them to write summoning him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 比克處，宜孫戰敗，走建寧，收集士卒，欲復處州。

translations.literal: By the time Chuzhou was taken, Yisun was defeated in battle, fled to Jianning, gathered soldiers, and wished to recover Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuzhou fell, Yisun was routed, fled to Jianning, gathered troops, and planned to retake Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 攻慶元，為耿再成所敗，還走建寧。

translations.literal: He attacked Qingyuan and was defeated by Geng Zaicheng, then fled back toward Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Qingyuan but was defeated by Geng Zaicheng and fled back toward Jianning.

sentences.zh: 半道遇鄉兵，被殺，部將李彥文葬之龍泉。

translations.literal: Halfway he encountered village militia and was killed; his subordinate general Li Yanwen buried him at Longquan.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway he was killed by village militia; his officer Li Yanwen buried him at Longquan.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其忠，遣使致祭，復其處州生祠。
