translations.literal: The founding emperor commended his loyalty, sent envoys to offer sacrifice, and restored his living shrine at Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The founder commended his loyalty, sent envoys to offer sacrifice, and restored his shrine at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 又祠福壽于應天，余闕于安慶，李黼于江州。

translations.literal: He also established shrines to Fushou at Yingtian, Yu Que at Anqing, and Li Fu at Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also established shrines to Fushou at Yingtian (Nanjing), Yu Que at Anqing, and Li Fu at Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 闕、黼事具《元史》。

translations.literal: The affairs of Que and Fu are fully recorded in the History of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The stories of Yu Que and Li Fu are recorded in full in the History of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 其後大軍北克益都，平章普顏不花不屈死。

translations.literal: Thereafter the great army took Yidu in the north; Grand Councillor Puyan Buhua died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: Later the main army took Yidu in the north; Grand Councillor Puyan Buhua died defiant.

sentences.zh: 克東昌，平章申榮自經死。

translations.literal: When Dongchang was taken, Grand Councillor Shen Rong hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: At Dongchang Grand Councillor Shen Rong hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 真定路達魯花赤鈒納錫彰聞王師取元都，朝服登城西崖，北面再拜，投崖死。

translations.literal: The Zhending circuit darughachi Qiana Xizhang, hearing the royal army had taken the Yuan capital, in court dress ascended the west cliff of the city, bowed twice facing north, and threw himself from the cliff to die.
translations.idiomatic: Zhending's darughachi Qiana Xizhang, hearing the Ming had taken Dadu, dressed in court robes, climbed the west cliff, bowed north, and leaped to his death.

sentences.zh: 克奉元，西台御史桑哥失裏與妻子俱投崖死，左丞拜泰古逃入終南山，郎中王可仰藥死，檢校阿失不花自經死。

translations.literal: When Fengyuan was taken, Western Platform Censor Sangeshili and his wife both threw themselves from a cliff to die; Left Chancellor Baitaigu fled into Zhongnan Mountain; Director Wang Keyang took poison to die; Inspector Ashibuhua hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengyuan (Xi'an) Censor Sangeshili and his wife leaped from a cliff; Left Chancellor Baitaigu fled to Zhongnan Mountain; Director Wang Keyang took poison; Inspector Ashibuhua hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 三原縣尹硃春謂其妻曰：「吾當死以報國。

translations.literal: The Sanyuan county magistrate Zhu Chun said to his wife: I ought to die to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: Sanyuan Magistrate Zhu Chun told his wife: "I must die to repay the state."

sentences.zh: 」妻曰：「君能盡忠，妾豈不能盡節。

translations.literal: His wife said: If you can exhaust loyalty, how can I not exhaust integrity?
translations.idiomatic: She said: "If you can give your life for loyalty, how can I not give mine for honor?"

sentences.zh: 」亦俱投繯死。

translations.literal: They both also threw themselves into nooses and died.
translations.idiomatic: They both hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 又大軍攻永州，右丞鄧祖勝固守，食盡力窮，仰藥死。

translations.literal: Again when the great army attacked Yongzhou, Right Chancellor Deng Zusheng held fast in defense; when food was exhausted and strength spent, he took poison looking upward and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the army attacked Yongzhou, Right Chancellor Deng Zusheng held out until food and strength were gone, then took poison.

sentences.zh: 克梧州，吏部尚書普顏帖木兒戰死，張翱赴水死。

translations.literal: When Wuzhou was taken, Minister of Personnel Puyan Temur died in battle; Zhang Ao went into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuzhou Minister of Personnel Puyan Temur fell in battle and Zhang Ao drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 克靖江，都事趙元隆、陳瑜、劉永錫，廉訪使僉事帖木兒不花，元帥元禿蠻，萬戶董醜漢，府判趙世傑皆自殺。

translations.literal: When Jingjiang was taken, Directors Zhao Yuanlong, Chen Yu, and Liu Yongxi, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Temur Buhua, Marshal Yuantuman, Myriarch Dong Chouhan, and Prefectural Judge Zhao Shijie all killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingjiang Directors Zhao Yuanlong, Chen Yu, and Liu Yongxi, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Temur Buhua, Marshal Yuantuman, Myriarch Dong Chouhan, and Prefectural Judge Zhao Shijie all took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 至如劉福通、徐壽輝、陳友諒等所破郡縣，守吏將帥多死節者，已見《元史》，不具載，載其見《明實錄》者。

translations.literal: As for prefectures and counties taken by Liu Futong, Xu Shouhui, Chen Youliang, and others—defending officials and generals who died for their integrity are many and already appear in the History of Yuan; they are not fully recorded here—only those appearing in the Veritable Records of Ming are recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The many officials who died defending prefectures taken by Liu Futong, Xu Shouhui, Chen Youliang, and others are recorded in the History of Yuan and are not repeated here; only those noted in the Ming Veritable Records are included.

sentences.zh: 又有劉諶，江西人，為仁壽教官。

translations.literal: There was also Liu Chen, a man of Jiangxi, who was an instructor at Renshou.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Liu Chen of Jiangxi, an instructor at Renshou.

sentences.zh: 明玉珍入蜀，棄官隱瀘州。

translations.literal: When Ming Yuzhen entered Shu, he abandoned office and hid at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming Yuzhen entered Sichuan, he resigned and went into hiding at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 玉珍欲官之，不就。

translations.literal: Yuzhen wished to give him office; he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Yuzhen offered him office; he refused.

sentences.zh: 鳳山趙善璞隱深山，明玉珍聘為學士，亦不就。

translations.literal: Zhao Shanpu of Fengshan hid in deep mountains; Ming Yuzhen engaged him as academician; he also would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shanpu of Fengshan lived as a recluse in the mountains; Ming Yuzhen offered him a post as academician, but he too refused.

sentences.zh: 而張士誠破平江時，參軍楊椿挺身戰，刃交於胸，嗔目怒駡死，妻亦自經。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shicheng's Pingjiang was taken, staff officer Yang Chun threw himself into battle; blades crossed at his chest; he glared with angry eyes and cursed until he died; his wife also hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shicheng's Pingjiang fell, staff officer Yang Chun fought to the death with blades in his chest, glaring and cursing his enemies; his wife hanged herself as well.

sentences.zh: 士誠又以書幣征故左司員外郎楊乘於松江，乘具酒醴告祖禰，顧西日晴明，曰：「人生晚節，如是足矣。

translations.literal: Shicheng also with letter and gifts summoned the former Left Secretariat Vice Director Yang Cheng at Songjiang; Cheng prepared wine and libations to inform his ancestors, looked at the clear western sun, and said: A man's late integrity—this is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng also summoned former Left Secretariat Vice Director Yang Cheng at Songjiang with gifts; Yang offered wine to his ancestors, looked at the clear western sun, and said: "A man's final honor—this is enough."

sentences.zh: 」夜分自經死。

translations.literal: At midnight he hanged himself to die.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 其親籓死事最烈者，有雲南梁王。

translations.literal: Among collateral princes whose deaths for the cause were most fierce was the Prince of Liang in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Among the collateral princes, the most resolute martyr was the Prince of Liang in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 把匝剌瓦爾密

translations.literal: Bazalawaermi.
translations.idiomatic: Bazalawaermi

sentences.zh: 梁王把匝剌瓦爾密，元世祖第五子雲南王忽哥赤之裔也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang Bazalawaermi was a descendant of Hugachi, Prince of Yunnan, the fifth son of Kublai Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Liang Bazalawaermi was a descendant of Hugachi, Prince of Yunnan, fifth son of Kublai Khan.

sentences.zh: 封梁王，仍鎮雲南。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang and still guarded Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang and continued to rule Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 順帝之世，天下多故，雲南僻遠，王撫治有威惠。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shundi's reign the realm had many troubles; Yunnan was remote and distant; the prince governed with authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Shundi's reign, while turmoil engulfed the realm, remote Yunnan remained stable under the prince's firm and benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 至正二十三年，明玉珍僭號於蜀，遣兵三道來攻，王走營金馬山。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Zhizheng, Ming Yuzhen usurped a title in Shu and sent troops in three columns to attack; the prince fled to encamp at Golden Horse Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng year 23 (1363), Ming Yuzhen declared himself in Sichuan and sent three columns against Yunnan; the prince withdrew to Golden Horse Mountain.

sentences.zh: 明年以大理兵迎戰，玉珍兵敗退。

translations.literal: The next year he met the attack with Dali troops; Yuzhen's army was defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he met them with Dali troops and routed Ming Yuzhen's army.

sentences.zh: 久之，順帝北去，大都不守，中國無元尺寸地，而王守雲南自若；

translations.literal: After a long time Emperor Shundi went north; Dadu was not held; in China there was not a span of Yuan territory—yet the prince guarded Yunnan as before;
translations.idiomatic: In time Emperor Shundi fled north, Dadu fell, and not a span of Yuan territory remained in China—yet the prince held Yunnan as before;

sentences.zh: 歲遣使自塞外達元帝行在，執臣節如故。

translations.literal: each year he sent envoys from beyond the passes to reach the Yuan emperor's mobile court, maintaining ministerial integrity as before.
translations.idiomatic: each year he sent envoys beyond the frontier to the Yuan emperor's court, maintaining his loyalty as before.

sentences.zh: 未幾，明師平四川，天下大定。

translations.literal: Before long Ming troops pacified Sichuan and the realm was largely settled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ming forces pacified Sichuan and the empire was largely settled.

sentences.zh: 太祖以雲南險僻，不欲用兵。

translations.literal: The founding emperor, because Yunnan was perilous and remote, did not wish to use troops.
translations.idiomatic: The founder, seeing Yunnan as remote and difficult, wished to avoid war.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，北平守將以所得王遣往漠北使者蘇成來獻，太祖乃命待制王禕齎詔偕成往招諭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year the Beiping defending general presented Su Cheng, an envoy the prince had sent toward the northern deserts whom he had captured; the founding emperor then ordered Academician Wang Yi to carry an edict and go with Cheng to summon and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the Beiping garrison presented Su Cheng, an envoy the prince had sent to the northern steppe whom they had captured; the founder ordered Academician Wang Yi to carry an edict and go with Cheng to offer terms.

sentences.zh: 王待禕以禮。

translations.literal: The prince received Yi with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The prince received Wang Yi with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 會元嗣君遣使脫脫來征餉，脫脫疑王有他意，因脅以危語。

translations.literal: It happened that the Yuan successor sovereign sent the envoy Toto to collect supplies; Toto suspected the prince of other intentions and therefore threatened him with dire words.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan heir's envoy Toto arrived to collect tribute; suspecting the prince of disloyalty, Toto threatened him.

sentences.zh: 王遂殺禕而以禮斂之。

translations.literal: The prince then killed Yi but buried him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then killed Wang Yi but buried him with full honors.

sentences.zh: 逾三年，太祖復遣湖廣參政吳雲偕大軍所獲雲南使臣鐵知院等往。

translations.literal: After more than three years the founding emperor again sent Huguang Vice Administrator Wu Yun together with Tiezhiyuan and other Yunnan envoys captured by the great army.
translations.idiomatic: More than three years later the founder sent Huguang Vice Administrator Wu Yun with Tiezhiyuan and other captured Yunnan envoys.

sentences.zh: 知院以己奉使被執，誘雲改制書紿王。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan, because he himself had been on a mission and was captured, induced Yun to alter the edict document to deceive the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Tiezhiyuan, having himself been captured on a mission, persuaded Wu Yun to alter the edict to deceive the prince.

sentences.zh: 雲不從，被殺。

translations.literal: Yun would not comply and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yun refused and was killed.

sentences.zh: 王聞雲死，收其骨，送蜀給孤寺。

translations.literal: When the prince heard Yun had died, he gathered his bones and sent them to Shu to be given to a temple for the orphaned dead.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Wu Yun's death, the prince gathered his remains and sent them to a temple in Sichuan for proper burial.

sentences.zh: 太祖知王終不可以諭降，乃命傅友德為征南將軍，藍玉、沐英為副，帥師征之。

translations.literal: The founding emperor knew the prince in the end could not be persuaded to surrender; he then appointed Fu Youde Southern Campaign General, with Lan Yu and Mu Ying as deputies, to command troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the prince would never submit, the founder appointed Fu Youde Southern Campaign General, with Lan Yu and Mu Ying as deputies, to lead the expedition.

sentences.zh: 洪武十四年十二月下普定。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of Hongwu they descended on Puding.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Hongwu year 14 (1381) they took Puding.

sentences.zh: 王遣司徒平章達裏麻率兵駐曲靖。

translations.literal: The prince sent Minister and Grand Councillor Dalima to lead troops stationed at Qujing.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sent Minister and Grand Councillor Dalima with troops to hold Qujing.

sentences.zh: 沐英引軍疾趨，乘霧抵白石江。

translations.literal: Mu Ying led troops in a rapid advance, using the fog to reach Baishi River.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Ying advanced rapidly through the fog to Baishi River.

sentences.zh: 霧解，達裏麻望見大驚。

translations.literal: When the fog lifted, Dalima saw them and was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the fog lifted, Dalima saw the Ming army and was terrified.

sentences.zh: 友德等率兵進擊，達裏麻兵潰被擒。

translations.literal: Youde and others led troops forward in attack; Dalima's army collapsed and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youde attacked; Dalima's army collapsed and he was captured.

sentences.zh: 先是，王以女妻大理酋段得功，嘗倚其兵力，後以疑殺之，遂失大理援。

translations.literal: Earlier the prince had given his daughter in marriage to the Dali chieftain Duan Degong and once relied on his military strength; later on suspicion he killed him, and thus lost Dali's support.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the prince had married his daughter to the Dali chieftain Duan Degong and relied on Dali's strength; later, suspecting treason, he killed Duan and lost Dali's support.

sentences.zh: 至是達裏麻敗，失精甲十余萬。

translations.literal: At this time Dalima was defeated and more than one hundred thousand elite armored troops were lost.
translations.idiomatic: With Dalima's defeat the prince lost more than one hundred thousand elite troops.

sentences.zh: 王知事不可為，走普寧州之忽納砦，焚其龍衣，驅妻子赴滇池死。

translations.literal: The prince knew the affair could not be accomplished; he fled to Hunazhai in Puning Prefecture, burned his dragon robes, and drove his wife and children to die in Dianchi Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that all was lost, the prince fled to Hunazhai in Puning, burned his imperial robes, and drove his wife and children into Dianchi Lake to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 遂與左丞達的、右丞驢兒夜入草舍，俱自經。

translations.literal: He then with Left Chancellor Dadi and Right Chancellor Lü'er entered a thatched hut by night and all hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: That night he entered a hut with Left Chancellor Dadi and Right Chancellor Lü'er, and all three hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 太祖遷其家屬于耽羅。

translations.literal: The founding emperor relocated his family members to Tamna.
translations.idiomatic: The founder relocated his surviving family to Jeju (Tamna).

sentences.zh: 贊曰：洪武九年，方穀珍死，宋濂奉敕撰墓碑，于一時群雄，皆直書其名，獨至察罕，曰齊國李忠襄王，順逆之理昭然可見矣。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: In the ninth year of Hongwu, Fang Guozhen died; Song Lian received an imperial command to compose his tomb inscription; of the contending warlords of the time he wrote all their names plainly—only for Chaghan he wrote Prince Li, Loyal and Commendable King of Qi; the principle of obedience and rebellion is plainly visible.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In Hongwu year 9 (1376), when Fang Guozhen died, Song Lian was ordered to compose his tomb inscription; of all the warlords of the age he recorded their names plainly—only for Chaghan Temur did he write "Prince Li, Loyal and Commendable King of Qi." The court's judgment of loyalty and treason could not be clearer.

sentences.zh: 擴廓百戰不屈，欲繼先志，而齎恨以死。

translations.literal: Kuokuotiemuer fought a hundred battles without yielding, wished to continue his predecessor's will, yet died bearing resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Kuokuotiemuer fought countless battles without yielding, striving to carry on Chaghan Temur's cause, yet died with his purpose unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 友定不作何真之偷生，梁王恥為納哈出之背國，要皆元之忠臣也。

translations.literal: Youding did not do as He Zhen and cling to life; the Prince of Liang was ashamed to be like Nahachu and betray his state—in the main all were loyal ministers of the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youding refused the craven survival of He Zhen; the Prince of Liang scorned Nahachu's betrayal of his country—all were loyal servants of the Yuan in the end.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰「其儀一兮，心如結兮」，《易》曰「苦節悔亡」，其伯顏子中、蔡子英之謂歟。

translations.literal: The Odes says, Their deportment is uniform; their hearts are knotted; the Changes says, Bitter integrity—regret vanishes—is this not meant of Bayan Zizhong and Cai Ziying?
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says, "Their bearing is uniform; their hearts are bound as with a knot"; the Changes says, "Bitter integrity, yet no regret"—surely this describes Bayan Zizhong and Cai Ziying.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂元歸塞外，一時從臣必有賦《式微》之章於沙漠之表者，惜其姓字湮沒，不得見於人間。

translations.literal: It has been said that when the Yuan returned beyond the frontier passes, among the followers of the time there must have been those who composed chapters of "Decline" on the desert's edge—pity that their surnames and names were lost and cannot be seen in the human world.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan withdrew beyond the frontier, surely some loyal followers composed laments like "Decline" on the desert's edge—yet their names are lost and their verses never reached the world.

sentences.zh: 然則若子英者，又豈非厚幸哉！

translations.literal: Yet then one such as Ziying—was he not also greatly fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: Yet for one such as Cai Ziying, was that not the greatest fortune of all!
